question: 72 + 18 − (26 + 17) + 44 × 2 − 33 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 102.

GIVEN

• 72 + 18 − (26 + 17) + 44 × 2 − 33

SOLUTION

• Bracket: 26 + 17 = 43.

• Multiply: 44 × 2 = 88.

• 72 + 18 − 43 + 88 − 33 = 90 − 43 + 88 − 33 = 47 + 88 − 33 = 135 − 33 = 102.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Group additions and subtractions: (72 + 18 + 88) − (43 + 33) = 178 − 76 = 102 in one glance.

NOTE

• Always apply BODMAS: Brackets → Orders → Division/Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction, left to right.

question: 79 + 28 − 44 + 17 × 2 + (33 ÷ 3) + 19 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 127.

GIVEN

• 79 + 28 − 44 + 17 × 2 + (33 ÷ 3) + 19

SOLUTION

• Bracket/Division: 33 ÷ 3 = 11.

• Multiply: 17 × 2 = 34.

• 79 + 28 − 44 + 34 + 11 + 19 = 107 − 44 + 34 + 11 + 19 = 63 + 34 + 11 + 19 = 127.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add the positives (79 + 28 + 34 + 11 + 19 = 171) and subtract 44: 171 − 44 = 127.

NOTE

• In BODMAS, division and multiplication rank above addition and subtraction, so resolve 33 ÷ 3 and 17 × 2 first.

question:
The line chart given below shows the sales of 5 items I1, I2, I3, I4 and I5 in a month.

Sales of I3 are what percent of combined sales of I1 and I4?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 58.95%.

GIVEN

• Sales: I1 = 45, I3 = 56, I4 = 50.

SOLUTION

• Combined sales of I1 and I4 = 45 + 50 = 95.

• Required % = (56 ÷ 95) × 100 = 58.947… ≈ 58.95%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 56/95 is just under 3/5 (=60%); a hair below 60% points straight to 58.95%.

NOTE

• 'A is what percent of B' = (A ÷ B) × 100; keep the base (B) as the denominator.

question:
The line chart given below shows the monthly petrol consumption (in litres) by 6 different cars CR1, CR2, CR3, CR4, CR5 and CR6.

The price per litre of petrol is Rs. 105.

P = Total monthly expenditure (in Rs.) on petrol for CR1 and CR4.

Q = Total monthly expenditure (in Rs.) on petrol for CR3 and CR6.

What is the value (in Rs.) of Q − P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 2100.

GIVEN

• Litres — CR1 = 74, CR4 = 60, CR3 = 79, CR6 = 75; price = Rs. 105/litre.

SOLUTION

• P litres = 74 + 60 = 134; Q litres = 79 + 75 = 154.

• Q − P (litres) = 154 − 134 = 20.

• Q − P (Rs.) = 20 × 105 = 2100.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Don't compute P and Q separately — take the litre difference (154 − 134 = 20) then multiply once by 105 = 2100.

NOTE

• When a common rate applies, subtract the quantities first and multiply by the rate at the end to save steps.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of milk shops in 6 towns. The data is presented in the terms of percent.

Number of milk shops in town A are what percent of number of milk shops in town F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 66.67%.

GIVEN

• Town A = 12%, Town F = 18%.

SOLUTION

• Required % = (A ÷ F) × 100 = (12 ÷ 18) × 100.

• = (2 ÷ 3) × 100 = 66.67%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 12/18 cancels to 2/3, and 2/3 is the standard 66.67% — no long division needed.

NOTE

• In a percentage pie, the actual totals cancel, so 'A as % of F' = A% ÷ F% × 100.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the number of laptops sold by the given 5 shops.

What are the total number of laptops sold by these 5 shops?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 700.

GIVEN

• Laptops — A = 120, B = 150, C = 110, D = 180, E = 140.

SOLUTION

• Total = 120 + 150 + 110 + 180 + 140.

• = 270 + 110 + 180 + 140 = 380 + 180 + 140 = 700.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Pair to round numbers: (120 + 180) + (150 + 150 approx) — actually (120+180)=300, (110+140)=250, +150 = 700.

NOTE

• For 'total' bar-graph questions just add all bar heights; pairing values into round sums reduces slips.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the selling price of 6 given articles.

Selling price = Cost price × [1 + (Profit%/100)]

Profit earned on article F is 30 percent. What is the cost price of article F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 461.54.

GIVEN

• Selling price of F = 600, Profit% = 30.

SOLUTION

• SP = CP × [1 + 30/100] = CP × 1.3.

• CP = 600 ÷ 1.3 = 6000 ÷ 13 = 461.54 (approx).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• At 30% profit, CP = SP × 10/13; 600 × 10/13 = 6000/13 ≈ 461.54.

NOTE

• CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%); for 30% profit the multiplier is 10/13.

question: The ratio of two numbers is 3:4, and their sum is 84. What is the ratio of their squares?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 9:16.

GIVEN

• Ratio of numbers = 3 : 4, sum = 84.

SOLUTION

• Numbers = 3k and 4k, with 7k = 84 → k = 12, so 36 and 48.

• Ratio of squares = 3² : 4² = 9 : 16 (=1296 : 2304 = 9:16).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The ratio of squares is just the square of each ratio term: 3² : 4² = 9 : 16 — the sum 84 is not even needed.

NOTE

• If numbers are in ratio a : b, their squares are in ratio a² : b² and cubes in a³ : b³.

question: Find the approximate value of:

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 151.

GIVEN

• (169.89 × 101.96)/(16.93 × 33.98) + (198.11 × 120.87)/(32.89 × √35.97).

SOLUTION

• Round: first term ≈ (170 × 102)/(17 × 34) = 17340/578 = 30.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

NOTE

• In approximation questions, round to convenient integers first (and √36 = 6) before simplifying.

question: If the square of a number is increased by 56, the result is 225. Find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 13.

GIVEN

• x² + 56 = 225.

SOLUTION

• x² = 225 − 56 = 169.

• x = √169 = 13.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 225 is 15² and 169 is 13²; spotting 225 − 56 = 169 = 13² gives the answer instantly.

NOTE

• Memorise perfect squares up to 30² (13² = 169, 15² = 225) to solve such questions by inspection.

question: The average weight of P, Q, and R is 45 kg. If the average weight of P and Q is 40 kg, and that of Q and R is 43 kg, what is the weight of R?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 55 kg.

GIVEN

• Avg(P,Q,R) = 45, Avg(P,Q) = 40, Avg(Q,R) = 43.

SOLUTION

• P + Q + R = 3 × 45 = 135; P + Q = 2 × 40 = 80.

• R = 135 − 80 = 55 kg.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• R = (sum of all three) − (sum of P and Q) = 135 − 80 = 55; the Q+R data is only a decoy.

NOTE

• Sum = average × number of items; subtracting known subgroup totals isolates the unknown quickly.

question: Which of the following lies between (3/10) & (7/10)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 7/11.

GIVEN

• Interval: 3/10 = 0.3 to 7/10 = 0.7.

SOLUTION

• 8/9 = 0.889, 13/17 = 0.765, 10/11 = 0.909 — all above 0.7.

• 7/11 = 0.636, which lies between 0.3 and 0.7 = 7/11.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Convert each option to a decimal and keep only the one under 0.7; only 7/11 (≈0.64) qualifies.

NOTE

• To compare fractions fast, convert to decimals or cross-multiply against the boundary values.

question:
The table given below shows the number of tiffins sold by 6 shops.

Total number of tiffins sold by M1 and M2 are how much less than the total number of tiffins sold by M5 and M6?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 140.

GIVEN

• M1 = 100, M2 = 120, M5 = 200, M6 = 160.

SOLUTION

• M1 + M2 = 100 + 120 = 220.

• M5 + M6 = 200 + 160 = 360.

• Difference = 360 − 220 = 140.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Pair the differences: (200 − 100) + (160 − 120) = 100 + 40 = 140.

NOTE

• 'How much less' means larger group total minus smaller group total; read only the needed rows.

question:
The table given below shows the number of bottles of type B1, B2, B3, B4 and B5 manufactured by 2 companies P and Q.

R1 = Average number of B1 bottles manufactured by P and Q.

R2 = Average number of B4 bottles manufactured by P and Q.

What is the value of R2 − R1?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 40.

GIVEN

• B1: P = 100, Q = 20; B4: P = 60, Q = 140.

SOLUTION

• R1 = (100 + 20) ÷ 2 = 60.

• R2 = (60 + 140) ÷ 2 = 100.

• R2 − R1 = 100 − 60 = 40.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• R2 − R1 = [(B4 sum) − (B1 sum)] ÷ 2 = (200 − 120) ÷ 2 = 80 ÷ 2 = 40.

NOTE

• Difference of two averages over the same count = (difference of the totals) ÷ that count.

question: The sum of the three consecutive even numbers is 18. What is the product of the smallest and the largest of the three numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 32.

GIVEN

• Three consecutive even numbers with sum 18.

SOLUTION

• Middle number = 18 ÷ 3 = 6, so numbers are 4, 6, 8.

• Product of smallest and largest = 4 × 8 = 32.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Middle term = sum/3 = 6; smallest × largest = (6 − 2)(6 + 2) = 6² − 4 = 32.

NOTE

• For equally spaced numbers the middle term equals the mean; (a−d)(a+d) = a² − d² speeds the product.

question: Which of the following number is NOT divisible by 6?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 7342.

GIVEN

• Test divisibility by 6 (= divisible by both 2 and 3).

SOLUTION

• 7342: even, but digit sum 7+3+4+2 = 16, not divisible by 3 → NOT divisible by 6.

• 7482 (sum 21), 7128 (sum 18), 8136 (sum 18) are even and divisible by 3 → all divisible by 6.

• Hence the odd one out is 7342.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• All options are even, so only check the digit sum for divisibility by 3; only 7342 (sum 16) fails.

NOTE

• A number is divisible by 6 iff it is even AND its digit sum is divisible by 3.

question: 62P8 is divisible by 4. Which of the following cannot be the value of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• 62P8 is divisible by 4; find P that is impossible.

SOLUTION

• Divisibility by 4 depends on the last two digits 'P8'.

• P=0 → 08, P=2 → 28, P=6 → 68 are all divisible by 4; P=3 → 38 is not (38 ÷ 4 = 9.5).

• So P cannot be 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the last two digits matter: check which 'P8' is not a multiple of 4 — 38 fails, so P = 3.

NOTE

• A number is divisible by 4 iff the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

question: Average of 17 consecutive natural numbers starting with 'a' is x. What will be the average of 17 consecutive natural numbers starting with 'a + 6'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. x + 6.

GIVEN

• 17 consecutive numbers from 'a' have average x.

SOLUTION

• The average of consecutive numbers is the middle term: a + 8 = x.

• New set starts at a + 6, so its middle term = (a + 6) + 8 = x + 6.

• Hence new average = x + 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Shift every term up by 6 and the average also shifts up by exactly 6 → x + 6.

NOTE

• For consecutive numbers, average = middle term; adding a constant to each shifts the mean by that same constant.

question:
In following figure, XA is parallel to PQ. What is the value (in degrees) of angle YBP.

(Figure: X, Y, O, A lie on one straight line; PQ is a parallel line above with the ray PB passing through O down to B. Angle QPO = 145°, angle XYB = 115°.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 80.

GIVEN

• XA ∥ PQ, angle QPO = 145°, angle XYB = 115°.

SOLUTION

• Line PB cuts parallels PQ and XA, so angle POA = 180° − 145° = 35° (co-interior), giving angle YOB = 35°.

• At Y, angle BYO = 180° − 115° = 65° (linear pair on line XA).

• In triangle YOB, angle YBO = 180° − 65° − 35° = 80°; since P, O, B are collinear, angle YBP = 80°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• angle YBP = (180 − 145) + (180 − 115) − 20… simpler: use the two straight-line supplements 35° and 65°, then 180 − (35 + 65) = 80°.

NOTE

• With parallel lines, use co-interior/alternate angles to move angles onto the transversal, then apply the triangle angle-sum (180°).

question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. Angle BAE = 65 degrees and angle BEA = 55 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle CDE?

(Figure: a bowtie shape — B and A on the left, C and D on the right, meeting at centre E, with straight lines A–E–C and B–E–D. AB ∥ CD.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 60.

GIVEN

• AB ∥ CD, angle BAE = 65°, angle BEA = 55°.

SOLUTION

• In triangle ABE: angle CED = angle BEA = 55° (vertically opposite).

• AB ∥ CD with transversal AC gives angle DCE = angle BAE = 65° (alternate angles).

• In triangle CDE: angle CDE = 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Triangles ABE and CDE are similar (AB ∥ CD), so angle CDE = angle ABE = 180° − 65° − 55° = 60°.

NOTE

• Parallel sides across a crossing point create equal alternate angles and vertically opposite angles, making the two triangles equiangular.
